title: Add read-only Git proofs for worktrees: provesWorktree, closeReadiness, setupDeclared
description:
## Objective
Extend `server/git.ts` with `provesWorktree(dir, { gitCommonDir, baseCommit, leadDir })`, `closeReadiness(dir, { candidate, base })`, `setupDeclared(gitCommonDir, baseCommit)` and make candidate derivation work inside a linked worktree.

## Context
Paseo may silently branch from an existing branch (observed in the delta §9.1 probe) and runs repository setup in the background, so the runtime must prove every created worktree with Git and must know whether a repository declares setup.

## Scope
In scope:
- `provesWorktree`: common dir equals the project's, `HEAD` equals `baseCommit` exactly, tree clean, directory is not Lead's; distinct failure codes.
- `closeReadiness`: `clean-at-candidate` | `clean-at-base` | `dirty` | `unrecorded-commits`.
- `setupDeclared`: `git show <commit>:paseo.json`; returns absent | none | declared (non-empty `worktree.setup`).
- Tests with real temporary repositories and `git worktree add`.
Out of scope:
- Calling these from the controller.
- Any mutating Git command (never: clean, reset, stash, checkout, branch -D, worktree remove).

- test/runtime-git.test.ts

- Read-only Git only; existing `GitEvidence` style and error shapes.

## Acceptance Criteria (Validation / Definition of Done)
- Tests cover: exact base passes; moved HEAD, dirty tree, foreign common dir and Lead's own directory each fail distinctly; setup absent/empty/declared; each close-readiness outcome; candidate derivation in a linked worktree.
- `npm run verify` (typecheck → lint → test → build → packed-package test) passes.

## Primary Proof

title: Add the conservative scope checker server/domain/scope.ts with an oracle soundness test
description:
## Objective
Create `src/runtime-plugin/server/domain/scope.ts` exporting `parseScope`, `normalizeScope`, `overlaps(a,b)`, `reaches(scope, serialPath)` and `conforms(changedPaths, scopes)`, plus its test file.

## Context
Phase 2 lets several Peers write concurrently only when their declared write scopes cannot overlap. This checker is the scheduling evidence behind the `scope_overlap`, `serial_path` and `scope.exceeded` decisions; it is not access control.

## Scope
In scope:
- Grammar (delta §5.1): repository-relative POSIX paths of `/`-separated segments; a segment is a literal or uses only `*` (within a segment) and `?`; a whole segment may be `**`. Refuse absolute paths, empty entry, `.`/`..` segments, backslash, leading `!`, `{}`, `[]`, and anything over `shared/limits.ts` string limits — the refusal names the offending item.
- Normalisation: Unicode NFC, collapse repeated `/`, strip trailing `/`; every entry implicitly ends in `/**`; an empty scope list means `**` (whole repository).
- `overlaps`: segment-by-segment memoised recursion; `**` consumes zero or one segment of the other side; literal vs literal equal after case folding; literal vs pattern uses a small `*`/`?` matcher; pattern vs pattern is true unless fixed literal prefixes or suffixes provably differ (`a*` vs `b*`, `*.ts` vs `*.md`).
- `reaches`: true when a scope may match any path under a serial-only path. `conforms`: returns the changed paths not matched by any scope.
- Tests including an oracle: enumerate every path up to depth 4 over a small alphabet and assert `overlaps` never returns false where `node:path` `matchesGlob` finds a path matched by both.
Out of scope:
- Wiring into dispatch, events or handoff (later beads).
- Any third-party glob library (cannot ship in the plugin).

## Components Touched
- src/runtime-plugin/server/domain/scope.ts — new module
- test/runtime-scope.test.ts — new test file

## Dependencies / Prerequisites
- none

## Assumptions / Constraints
- Runtime server code may import only `@getpaseo/plugin*`, `zod` and `node:` modules (enforced by `test/runtime-plugin-boundary.test.ts`); only `server/paseo-port.ts` calls Paseo's SDK.
- Soundness is the contract: a false 'disjoint' is a defect, a false 'overlap' is acceptable. Case folding and NFC are applied before every comparison.
- `matchesGlob` is used only in tests as an oracle; the engine floor is Node 22.

title: Run the worktree dispatch lifecycle: lease, workspace, Git proof, Peer in workspace, first turn
description:
## Objective
Implement the success path of worktree dispatch per delta §6: `assignment.dispatch-requested` → `ownership.reserved` → `lease.reserved` (runtime-minted `wks_` id and `ws-<assignmentId>-e<epoch>` key, branch `paseo-room/<assignmentId>`, slug = lower-cased assignment id) → `workspace.create-requested` → create → Git proof → `workspace.create-succeeded` (or `workspace.create-refused` then close, no Peer) → identified Peer creation in the workspace with Lead as parent → binding proof comparing the snapshot's workspaceId to the lease's → `ownership.held` → generation → `run`.
